question: Under the same short time budget, can a greedy-seeded, CV-tuned swap local search place k monitors with higher coverage than default simulated annealing?
method: BFS-sampled subgraphs x several k; closed-neighbourhood coverage; random search on tuning instances with grouped CV; same wall-clock budget per instance; relative to HiGHS MILP incumbent.
metric_name: covered-node fraction relative to MILP reference value
baseline: Simulated-annealing swap metaheuristic with default parameters (T0=1, alpha=0.999) from a random start.
improved: Lazy-greedy initialisation + best-swap tabu local search with restarts; params from random search (12 configs, 3-fold grouped CV on tuning instances): {'tenure': 0, 'patience': 100, 'perturb': 0.4, 'n_out': 3}.
notes: n_rows is the edge count; n_train/n_test count instances (graph, k), split by sampled graph. Budget 2.0s per instance/method/seed; tuning used a shorter 0.3s budget. MILP time limit 20s, so reference may be sub-optimal and scores can exceed 1. Problem formulation (closed-neighbourhood coverage) is an assumption since the paper's exact model is unavailable. Wall-clock budgets make results machine-dependent. Small test set (3 graphs x 3 k); seed std is over per-seed means across test instances.
